title: 1.4 Make-up of the Nucleus: Subatomic Particles and Isotopes
description: Subatomic particles, atomic mass units, atomic number, mass number, isotopes, and average atomic mass

questions.question: Which particle did Rutherford discover in 1919 when alpha particles struck lighter elements such as nitrogen?
A proton is a nuclear particle having:
options: a positive charge equal in magnitude to that of the electron
a negative charge equal to that of the electron
twice the charge of the electron
questions.correctAnswer: a positive charge equal in magnitude to that of the electron

questions.question: The mass of a proton is approximately:
One atomic mass unit (amu) is defined as:
options: $1/12$ the mass of an atom of carbon-12
$1/12$ the mass of a hydrogen atom
questions.correctAnswer: $1/12$ the mass of an atom of carbon-12

The atomic number (Z) of an element equals:
options: the number of protons in the nucleus
the number of neutrons in the nucleus
the total number of protons and neutrons
the number of neutrons minus protons
questions.correctAnswer: the number of protons in the nucleus

questions.question: The mass number (A) of an atom equals:
options: the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus
the number of electrons in the atom
questions.correctAnswer: the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus

questions.question: Isotopes of an element are atoms that have:
options: different numbers of neutrons and different mass numbers
the same number of neutrons but different protons
questions.correctAnswer: different numbers of neutrons and different mass numbers

questions.question: All atoms of a particular element:
options: have the same number of neutrons

questions.question: All carbon atoms have how many protons in the nucleus?
What percentage of naturally occurring carbon atoms have six neutrons ($A = 12$)?
The isotope $^{13}$C of carbon contains how many neutrons in its nucleus?
How many naturally occurring isotopes does carbon have?
The average (relative) atomic mass of an element is obtained by:
options: averaging the isotopic masses weighted by their fractional abundances
dividing the mass number by the atomic number
adding all the isotopic masses together
taking the mass of the lightest isotope
questions.correctAnswer: averaging the isotopic masses weighted by their fractional abundances

questions.question: For an element with $n$ isotopes of relative masses $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_n$ and fractional abundances $f_1, f_2, \dots, f_n$, the average atomic mass is given by:
options: $A = A_1 f_1 + A_2 f_2 + \dots + A_n f_n$
questions.correctAnswer: $A = A_1 f_1 + A_2 f_2 + \dots + A_n f_n$
